node.title: Re: Why do I need a local variable in map function
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
s/// [id://1215373|returns] the number of substitutions made, so that's what that map block is returning. Although it's generally not considered good practice to modify the original list by modifying or assigning to $_ in a [doc://map] block, the first version could be written as map { $_ = quotemeta($_) . '$'; s/\\\*/.*/g; $_ } to achieve the desired result. Alternatively, as of Perl 5.14, you can say s///r to have the regex return the modified string, e.g. map { my $x = quotemeta($_) . '$'; $x =~ s/\\\*/.*/gr }.

Update: Note that your second regex includes /g, while your first one does not; I've added it to both my examples.

Update 2: Or even just map { quotemeta($_).'$' =~ s/\\\*/.*/gr } or map { "\Q$_\E\$" =~ s/\\\*/.*/gr }
